joc.goggles.seeker_table.no_marker: Right-click the map to place a marker
joc.ponder.balloon_intro.text_1: Hold Right-Click with a Deflated Balloon to blow it up
joc.ponder.balloon_intro.text_2: Balloons lift Simulated Contraptions without needing Hot Air
joc.ponder.balloon_intro.text_3: Each Balloon lifts the weight of 1.5 Stone Blocks, yet weighs only a quarter of one
joc.ponder.balloon_intro.text_4: Lift weakens as Air Pressure drops, so a Contraption overshoots, then bobs around the Altitude where Lift equals Weight
joc.ponder.balloon_intro.text_5: With far too much Lift it will climb past the Atmosphere, where its Balloons pop
joc.ponder.balloon_intro.text_6: Each Balloon pulls where it sits, so spread them evenly or the Contraption will tilt
joc.ponder.balloon_pop.text_1: Right-Click with Dye to repaint a Balloon
joc.ponder.balloon_pop.text_2: Touching Balloons of one color count as a single Envelope
joc.ponder.balloon_pop.text_3: An Arrow pops every connected Balloon of the same color at once
joc.ponder.balloon_pop.text_4: Other colors survive, so divide large Envelopes to keep some Lift
joc.ponder.gyroscopic_seat.header: Riding Steady in the Gyroscopic Seat
joc.ponder.gyroscopic_seat.text_1: The Gyroscopic Seat fills a 2×2×2 space on a Contraption
joc.ponder.gyroscopic_seat.text_2: Right-Click to climb into the middle of it
joc.ponder.gyroscopic_seat.text_3: As the Contraption rolls and pitches, the rings swing so the Seat stays level
joc.ponder.gyroscopic_seat.text_4: Your view stays steady, however rough the flight
joc.ponder.seeker_eye.header: Reading the Player's Gaze with the Seeker
joc.ponder.seeker_eye.text_1: An Eye of Ender makes the Seeker follow a Player's gaze instead of a Target
joc.ponder.seeker_eye.text_2: Right-Click with an empty hand to bind it to you, and again to let go
joc.ponder.seeker_eye.text_3: While bound, its sides output the direction you look, from any distance
joc.ponder.seeker_eye.text_4: Feed these into your Engines to steer a Contraption just by looking
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_1: The Seeker turns the direction of a Target into Redstone signals
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_2: Look through a Spyglass and Left-Click a block to mark it as the Target
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_3: Then Right-Click the Seeker to slot the Spyglass in
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_4: The sides turned toward the Target emit a signal
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_5: The more directly a side faces the Target, the stronger its signal
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_6: Right-Click with an empty hand to type coordinates, pick a Waypoint or switch between 3D and flat 2D tracking
joc.ponder.seeker_intro.text_7: Sneak and Right-Click to take the Spyglass back out
joc.ponder.seeker_linking.text_1: Right-Click a Seeker with a Seeker item to capture it
joc.ponder.seeker_linking.text_2: Right-Click a second Seeker to link them. Placing the held Seeker down links it too
joc.ponder.seeker_linking.text_3: Linked Seekers share their Target, so changing one retargets them all
joc.ponder.seeker_logic_core.header: Going Wireless with the Logic Core
joc.ponder.seeker_logic_core.text_1: Open Advanced Options in the Seeker's screen and place a Logic Core in its slot
joc.ponder.seeker_logic_core.text_2: The Seeker stops powering its sides...
joc.ponder.seeker_logic_core.text_3: ...and sends each side's signal over its own Redstone Link frequency instead
joc.ponder.seeker_modulating.text_1: A Modulating Linked Receiver makes the Seeker measure how far away the Target is
joc.ponder.seeker_modulating.text_2: Right-Click to set a Min and Max distance: full signal at Min, none past Max
joc.ponder.seeker_modulating.text_3: Every side outputs the same signal, and the Receiver spins faster as the Target gets closer
joc.ponder.seeker_table.header: Mapping the World on a Seeker Table
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_1: An exact rectangle of empty Seekers, 3×3 or larger, joins into a Seeker Table
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_2: Its surface draws a relief map of the land around it, rotating with the Contraption it sits on
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_3: Right-Click the map to pin a spot on it
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_4: An Iron Sword, Banner, Arrow or Torch leaves its own kind of Marker
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_5: Map Pins can also be thrown, and Arrows shot, to mark wherever they land
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_6: Use a Wrench to cycle the map's scale, from 1:8 up to 1:128
joc.ponder.seeker_table.text_7: Sneak and Right-Click to remove the Marker
joc.ponder.seeker_table_following.text_1: Right-Click the map with a Seeker item to capture the Table
joc.ponder.seeker_table_following.text_2: Then Right-Click a Seeker holding a Spyglass or Receiver. It now follows the Table
joc.ponder.seeker_table_following.text_3: Wherever you pin the map, the Seeker points to that spot in the World
joc.ponder.seeker_table_wall.header: Hanging a Seeker Table on a Wall
joc.ponder.seeker_table_wall.text_1: Seekers placed in an upright rectangle form a wall-mounted Table, facing the side you built it from
joc.ponder.seeker_table_wall.text_2: It works just like a flat Table, with the bottom edge of the map pointing the way the wall faces
joc.ponder.shatter_assembler_intro.heade: Breaking Structures Apart with the Shatter Assembler
joc.ponder.shatter_assembler_intro.text_: Place a Shatter Assembler onto any block of a Structure
Hold Right-Click, pull the lever all the way, then let go
Every connected Solid Block breaks away as its own Simulated Contraption
The ground counts as a Structure too, so keep it from touching Solid terrain
joc.ponder.shatter_assembler_solid.text_: The Assembler spreads from its Block through Solid Blocks that touch face to face
Blocks that aren't full and solid, such as Lanterns and Fences, are left out
So are Blocks that don't touch the rest
joc.ponder.symmetric_cross_sail_drag.hea: Steering Contraptions with Cross Sail Fins
joc.ponder.symmetric_cross_sail_drag.tex: Unlike Sails, Cross Sails produce no Lift, only Drag
Moving along their Axis, the Sails slip through the Air with no Drag at all
Moving across it, both faces catch the Air and Drag pushes back
A fin along the Hull lets a Contraption fly straight, while resisting drift sideways and vertically
Symmetric Cross Sails are two Sails crossed along one Axis, set by the direction you face
Right-Click a Cross Sail with another to extend it along its Axis
Right-Clicking with a regular Sail attaches it to the side, lined up with the Cross Sail
Right-Click with Dye to paint it, and keep clicking to spread to the Cross Sails beside it
